topic: Display advertising monetization (Google AdSense) — Japan market focus

benchmark_rates.notes: Japan is a Tier-1 (high-CPM) market comparable to US/Western Europe. General-content sites earn far below premium niches (finance, insurance, SaaS, career). RPM (revenue per 1000 pageviews) is the metric AdSense reports; CPM is the advertiser cost per 1000 impressions.

1k_visitors.practical_note: Below AdSense's $100 (~¥15,000) payout threshold; accumulates but no cash paid until threshold is crossed.

10k_visitors.practical_note: Clears payout threshold; realistic side-income tier.

100k_visitors.practical_note: Meaningful recurring income; scaling further depends on niche and ad layout/SEO.

time_lag_note.summary: Roughly 1.5–2 months between traffic occurring and cash received.
details: Earnings accrue during month N but are not finalized until ~the 10th–12th of month N+1 (after advertiser corrections/chargebacks).
Payment is then issued around the 21st–25th of month N+1 — i.e. net ~45–60 days after the traffic was served.
Minimum payout threshold is $100 (≈¥15,000); balances below it roll over and are never paid out until crossed.
New AdSense accounts have an additional ~30-day hold on the first payment.
Implication for forecasting: the revenue you 'see' in month N is realized in cash during month N+2.

key_caveats: RPM varies enormously by niche, traffic quality, geo (Japan desktop vs mobile), ad unit placement, and season (Q4 CPM spikes).
Ad blockers, bot traffic, and invalid-click filtering reduce effective RPM.
These are display-ad-only estimates; adding affiliate links, native ads, or sponsored posts multiplies monetization beyond AdSense.
Japanese content + Japan-based audience is required to capture Japan CPMs; foreign traffic earns at lower local rates.
sources: Google AdSense Help (support.google.com/adsense) — payout schedule, $100 threshold, RPM definition
Established AdSense benchmark literature (WordStream, MonetizeMore, Ezoic) for global RPM/CPM ranges; Japan treated as Tier-1 high-CPM market
